candidates.title: An AI agent pays Papa John's straight from a bank account, inside limits the customer set with Lloyds, in the FCA's sandbox
candidates.summary: In a trial within the UK Financial Conduct Authority's AI regulatory sandbox, Papa John's own AI agent took a customer's order and paid from the bank account linked to their Papa John's account, through TrueLayer and Lloyds' variable recurring payment APIs; TrueLayer says it is the first time an AI agent has paid a UK retailer this way. The customer's spending limits are set with the bank and the agent cannot exceed them; no card details are shared. The FCA had reminded firms building agents that week that existing rules apply.
candidates.why_it_matters: The mandate held by the bank, not the agent: the limit lives where the money is, and a regulator's sandbox watches. A European model for agentic payments to set beside the US banks pushing losses onto customers.

quote.text: Today it's pizza. Tomorrow it's everything else.
quote.by: Francesco Simoneschi, CEO and co-founder of TrueLayer, quoted by Tech.eu

claims_to_check: TrueLayer's, Lloyds' or the FCA's own announcement; 'first' is TrueLayer's claim

importance.reason: Same-day, European, regulator-supervised agent payment with bank-held limits.

candidates.title: Black Friday test: AI shopping agents make 0.4% of online orders as half of big retailers keep them out
candidates.summary: Bain & Co research cited by CNBC finds AI agent purchases were 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions and 0.2% of their value. Testing by London's Human Forward, reported by Bloomberg, found about half of big retailers do not let AI assistants shop their sites; Amazon still blocks Meta's Muse and is suing Perplexity over its Comet agent, while eBay, United and Kohl's restrict agents and Best Buy's terms disclaim responsibility for any 'Digital Agent'. A Visa test found 22 models failed 42.8% of runs on 15 shopping tasks.
candidates.why_it_matters: Behind the launches, the numbers: agents are barely buying yet, and the merchants writing their own rules for them are the reason.
claims_to_check: Bain's study (no sample or year given by TNW); Human Forward's test via Bloomberg; Visa's test

importance.reason: Useful numbers for the week's thread; mostly second-hand.

candidates.title: 88% of Portuguese workers now use AI agents at work, up from 58% in a year, Adecco finds; only 7% feel managers' empathy
candidates.summary: Adecco Group's Global Workforce of the Future 2026 (40,500 workers in 36 countries, 950 in Portugal) finds the share of Portuguese workers using AI agents at work rose from 58% to 88% in a year, against a 10-point rise globally, while only 7% say managers show empathy for the change's effect on their jobs (19% globally). Adecco Portugal's CEO Alexandra Andrade says introducing tools is not enough.
candidates.why_it_matters: Portugal adopting agents faster than the world, with a governance gap of its own: who explains the agents' mandate to the people working beside them.

quote.text: Não basta introduzir novas ferramentas e esperar que as pessoas se adaptem.
quote.by: Alexandra Andrade, CEO of Adecco Portugal, quoted by Jornal Económico

claims_to_check: Adecco's own report, and what it counts as 'using AI agents' (the 23 Nov Jornal de Negócios figure was 74% globally)

importance.reason: Portuguese, same-day, a striking figure that needs its definition checked.
